input.content: Anti-pattern (P0 correctness): "Simplifying" a compare-and-delete guard into an unconditional delete causes lost-update / wrong-eviction when the resource can be reassigned. Example: cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id) originally popped store.active[workspace_id] only if the active association's setup_id matched the one being cleaned up. Removing the `if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id` guard and calling store.active.pop(workspace_id, None) unconditionally evicts the CURRENT active setup when a stale/superseded setup is cleaned up after a newer setup took ownership of the same workspace. The stored setup_id in the active record is an ownership token — a guard that compares it before mutating must be preserved. Pattern to flag: removal of a check-then-act ownership guard before pop/delete/update on shared state keyed by a parent id.
